title: Chang'e 6 lunar far-side sample return
summary: The first mission to return samples from the far side of the Moon.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Chang'e 6 launched in May 2024 and returned 1,935.3 grams of lunar far-side material in June 2024, the first samples from that hemisphere. The mission required a relay satellite for communications and demonstrated precision landing, ascent and rendezvous. China has since invited international researchers to apply for access, using sample distribution as scientific diplomacy.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2024–2027
Confidence label Confirmed
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

  • Tiangong space station

Investment Exposure

Sample access is a soft-power instrument; the research output will shape lunar geology for a decade.

What Would Change The View

  • Allocation of samples to non-Chinese labs.
  • Follow-on Chang'e 7 and 8 landing results.
  • International research publications.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
